sanskrit: śośubhyamānaḥ kaunteya ānupūrvyān mahābhujaḥ astrāṇi tāni divyāni darśanāyopacakrame
english: Resplendent, O son of Kunti, the mighty-armed one began to display those divine weapons one by one for all to see.

sanskrit: atha prayokṣyamāṇena divyāny astrāṇi tena vai samākrāntā mahī padbhyāṃ samakampata sadrumā
english: As he was about to discharge those divine weapons, the earth, along with its trees, shook and trembled under his feet.

sanskrit: kṣubhitāḥ saritaś caiva tathaiva ca mahodadhiḥ śailāś cāpi vyaśīryanta na vavau ca samīraṇaḥ
english: The rivers were disturbed, the great ocean heaved, the mountains crumbled, and the wind ceased to blow.

sanskrit: na babhāse sahasrāṃśur na jajvāla ca pāvakaḥ na vedāḥ pratibhānti sma dvijātīnāṃ kathaṃ cana
english: The thousand-rayed sun ceased to shine, fire did not burn, and the Vedic hymns no longer came to the minds of the twice-born in any way.

sanskrit: antarbhūmigatā ye ca prāṇino janamejaya pīḍyamānāḥ samutthāya pāṇḍavaṃ paryavārayan
english: Those living beings that dwelt within the earth, O Janamejaya, rose up in their affliction and surrounded the son of Pandu.

sanskrit: vepamānāḥ prāñjalayas te sarve pihitānanāḥ dahyamānās tadāstrais tair yācanti sma dhanaṃjayam
english: Trembling, with hands joined in supplication, their faces covered, scorched by those weapons, they all beseeched Dhananjaya.

sanskrit: tato brahmarṣayaś caiva siddhāś caiva surarṣayaḥ jaṅgamāni ca bhūtāni sarvāṇy evāvatasthire
english: Then the brahmarshis, the siddhas, the divine sages, and all mobile creatures stood still.

sanskrit: rājarṣayaś ca pravarās tathaiva ca divaukasaḥ yakṣarākṣasagandharvās tathaiva ca patatriṇaḥ
english: The foremost royal sages, the dwellers of heaven, the yakshas, rakshasas, gandharvas, and the birds all gathered there likewise.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmahaś caiva lokapālāś ca sarvaśaḥ bhagavāṃś ca mahādevaḥ sagaṇo 'bhyāyayau tadā
english: Then the Grandfather Brahma, all the guardians of the worlds, and the blessed Mahadeva together with his host came there.

sanskrit: tato vāyur mahārāja divyair mālyaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ abhitaḥ pāṇḍavāṃś citrair avacakre samantataḥ
english: Then the wind, O great king, showered variegated divine garlands of sweet fragrance all around and upon the Pandavas on every side.

sanskrit: jaguś ca gāthā vividhā gandharvāḥ suracoditāḥ nanṛtuḥ saṃghaśaś caiva rājann apsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: The gandharvas, urged on by the gods, sang various songs, and the hosts of apsaras danced in groups, O king.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tumule kāle nāradaḥ suracoditaḥ āgamyāha vacaḥ pārthaṃ śravaṇīyam idaṃ nṛpa
english: In that tumultuous moment, Narada, sent by the gods, came and spoke these words worthy of hearing to the son of Pritha, O king.

sanskrit: arjunārjuna mā yuṅkṣva divyāny astrāṇi bhārata naitāni niradhiṣṭhāne prayujyante kadā cana
english: "Arjuna, Arjuna, do not discharge the divine weapons, O descendant of Bharata — these are never to be used against a target that does not warrant them.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhāne na vānārtaḥ prayuñjīta kadā cana prayoge sumahān doṣo hy astrāṇāṃ kurunandana
english: Nor should one who is not in distress ever use them even against a fitting target, for the improper employment of these weapons brings the gravest of faults, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: etāni rakṣyamāṇāni dhanaṃjaya yathāgamam balavanti sukhārhāṇi bhaviṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: If these are guarded in accordance with the rules by which they were received, O Dhananjaya, they will remain potent and bring happiness — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: arakṣyamāṇāny etāni trailokyasyāpi pāṇḍava bhavanti sma vināśāya maivaṃ bhūyaḥ kṛthāḥ kva cit
english: If not guarded, these weapons bring ruin even to the three worlds, O son of Pandu. Do not do this again anywhere."

sanskrit: ajātaśatro tvaṃ caiva drakṣyase tāni saṃyuge yojyamānāni pārthena dviṣatām avamardane
english: "You, O one without enemies, shall see those weapons employed by the son of Pritha in battle for the crushing of foes."

sanskrit: nivāryātha tataḥ pārthaṃ sarve devā yathāgatam jagmur anye ca ye tatra samājagmur nararṣabha
english: Having thus restrained the son of Pritha, all the gods departed as they had come, and so did the others who had assembled there, O bull among men.

sanskrit: teṣu sarveṣu kauravya pratiyāteṣu pāṇḍavāḥ tasminn eva vane hṛṣṭās ta ūṣuḥ saha kṛṣṇayā
english: When all of them had departed, O descendant of the Kurus, the Pandavas along with Krishna dwelt joyfully in that very forest.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca tasmin kṛtāstre rathināṃ pradhāne; pratyāgate bhavanād vṛtrahantuḥ ataḥ paraṃ kim akurvanta pārthāḥ; sametya śūreṇa dhanaṃjayena
english: Janamejaya said: "After that foremost of chariot-warriors, having mastered the weapons, had returned from the abode of the slayer of Vritra, what did the sons of Pritha do thereafter, having been reunited with the heroic Dhananjaya?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vaneṣu teṣv eva tu te narendrāḥ; sahārjunenendrasamena vīrāḥ tasmiṃś ca śailapravare suramye; dhaneśvarākrīḍagatā vijahruḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: "Those lords of men, those heroes, together with Arjuna who was equal to Indra himself, sported and took their ease in that excellent and beautiful mountain region, journeying to the pleasure-grounds of the lord of wealth."

sanskrit: veśmāni tāny apratimāni paśyan; krīḍāś ca nānādrumasaṃnikarṣāḥ cacāra dhanvī bahudhā narendraḥ; so 'streṣu yattaḥ satataṃ kirīṭī
english: Beholding those incomparable mansions and the sports near the diverse trees, the diademed archer, that lord among men, ever intent upon his weapons, roamed about in many directions.

sanskrit: avāpya vāsaṃ naradevaputrāḥ; prasādajaṃ vaiśravaṇasya rājñaḥ na prāṇināṃ te spṛhayanti rājañ; śivaś ca kālaḥ sa babhūva teṣām
english: Having obtained the dwelling born of the favour of king Vaisravana, those sons of the lord of men envied no living being, O king, and their time there was auspicious.

sanskrit: sametya pārthena yathaikarātram; ūṣuḥ samās tatra tadā catasraḥ pūrvāś ca ṣaṭ tā daśa pāṇḍavānāṃ; śivā babhūvur vasatāṃ vaneṣu
english: Having been reunited with the son of Pritha as though it were but a single night, they dwelt there for four years; and those ten years altogether — the six previous and these four — passed auspiciously for the Pandavas residing in the forests.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd vāyusutas tarasvī; jiṣṇuś ca rājānam upopaviśya yamau ca vīrau surarājakalpāv; ekāntam āsthāya hitaṃ priyaṃ ca
english: Then the swift son of Vayu, and Jishnu, and the two valiant twins, equal to the king of the gods, seated themselves beside the king in a private place and spoke words that were both beneficial and dear.

sanskrit: tava pratijñāṃ kururāja satyāṃ; cikīrṣamāṇās tvadanu priyaṃ ca tato 'nugacchāma vanāny apāsya; suyodhanaṃ sānucaraṃ nihantum
english: "Wishing to fulfil your true vow, O king of the Kurus, and to do what is dear to you, let us leave these forests and follow you to slay Suyodhana along with his followers."

sanskrit: ekādaśaṃ varṣam idaṃ vasāmaḥ; suyodhanāyādhamabuddhiśīlam; ajñātavāsaṃ sukham āpnuyāmaḥ
english: "This is the eleventh year we have dwelt here, deprived of our comforts by Suyodhana. Having deceived that one of base mind and character, let us happily pass our year of incognito."

sanskrit: tavājñayā pārthiva nirviśaṅkā; vihāya mānaṃ vicaran vanāni samīpavāsena vilobhitās te; jñāsyanti nāsmān apakṛṣṭadeśān
english: "Under your command, O king, roaming through the forests without fear, laying aside our pride, those who are tempted by our proximity to them will not recognize us when we are in a remote region."

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraṃ taṃ tu vihṛtya gūḍhaṃ; narādhamaṃ taṃ sukham uddharema niryātya vairaṃ saphalaṃ sapuṣpaṃ; tasmai narendrādhamapūruṣāya
english: "Having passed that year in concealment, let us destroy that vilest of men in happiness, exacting our enmity in full — with fruit and flower both — upon that most contemptible of kings and men."

sanskrit: suyodhanāyānucarair vṛtāya; tato mahīm āhara dharmarāja svargopamaṃ śailam imaṃ caradbhiḥ; śakyo vihantuṃ naradeva śokaḥ
english: "Then, O king of righteousness, reclaim the earth from Suyodhana surrounded by his followers; roaming this mountain that resembles heaven, the grief of a lord of men can be dispelled."

sanskrit: kīrtiś ca te bhārata puṇyagandhā; naśyeta lokeṣu carācareṣu tat prāpya rājyaṃ kurupuṃgavānāṃ; śakyaṃ mahat prāptam atha kriyāś ca
english: "Your fame, fragrant with virtue, O descendant of Bharata, would perish in the worlds of the moving and the unmoving; having regained the kingdom of the bull of the Kurus, great deeds can be performed."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu śakyaṃ satataṃ narendra; prāptuṃ tvayā yal labhase kuberāt kuruṣva buddhiṃ dviṣatāṃ vadhāya; kṛtāgasāṃ bhārata nigrahe ca
english: "This which you have received from Kubera is ever within reach for you, O lord of men. Make up your mind to slay the enemies and to subdue those who have wronged you, O descendant of Bharata."

sanskrit: tejas tavograṃ na saheta rājan; sametya sākṣād api vajrapāṇiḥ na hi vyathāṃ jātu kariṣyatas tau; sametya devair api dharmarāja
english: "Your fierce energy could not be endured even by the wielder of the thunderbolt himself were he to face you directly, O king; those two would never suffer distress even if they faced the gods themselves, O king of righteousness."

sanskrit: tvadarthasiddhyartham abhipravṛttau; suparṇaketuś ca śineś ca naptā yathaiva kṛṣṇo 'pratimo balena; tathaiva rājan sa śinipravīraḥ
english: "Both are engaged for the attainment of your purpose — he whose banner bears the Garuda eagle, and the grandson of Shini; just as Krishna is matchless in strength, so too, O king, is that foremost hero of Shini's line."

sanskrit: tavārthasiddhyartham abhipravṛttau; yathaiva kṛṣṇaḥ saha yādavais taiḥ tathaiva cāvāṃ naradevavarya; yamau ca vīrau kṛtinau prayoge tvadarthayogaprabhavapradhānāḥ; samaṃ kariṣyāma parān sametya
english: "Just as Krishna along with those Yadavas is engaged for the achievement of your ends, so too are we, O foremost of lords of men — and the two valiant twins, skilled in action — all of us, whose chief purpose springs from devotion to your cause, will together make the enemies equal to the ground."

sanskrit: tatas tad ājñāya mataṃ mahātmā; teṣāṃ sa dharmasya suto variṣṭhaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ vaiśravaṇādhivāsaṃ; cakāra dharmārthavid uttamaujaḥ
english: Then the great-souled, most excellent son of Dharma, understanding their intention, he who knew the purposes of righteousness and was of the highest valour, circumambulated the abode of Vaisravana.

sanskrit: āmantrya veśmāni nadīḥ sarāṃsi; sarvāṇi rakṣāṃsi ca dharmarājaḥ yathāgataṃ mārgam avekṣamāṇaḥ; punar giriṃ caiva nirīkṣamāṇaḥ
english: The king of righteousness took leave of the mansions, the rivers, the lakes, and all the guardian spirits, looking back along the road by which they had come, and gazing once more at the mountain.

sanskrit: samāptakarmā sahitaḥ suhṛdbhir; jitvā sapatnān pratilabhya rājyam śailendra bhūyas tapase dhṛtātmā; draṣṭā tavāsmīti matiṃ cakāra
english: "Having completed my task, together with my friends, having conquered my enemies and recovered my kingdom, I shall return again, O lord of mountains, with steadfast soul devoted to austerity, and see you again" — thus he resolved in his mind.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ sa sarvair anujair dvijaiś ca; tenaiva mārgeṇa patiḥ kurūṇām uvāha cainān sagaṇāṃs tathaiva; ghaṭotkacaḥ parvatanirjhareṣu
english: Accompanied by all his younger brothers and the brahmins, the lord of the Kurus went by that same road; and Ghatotkacha likewise carried them all along with their retinues through the mountain torrents.

sanskrit: tān prasthitān prītimanā maharṣiḥ; piteva putrān anuśiṣya sarvān sa lomaśaḥ prītamanā jagāma; divaukasāṃ puṇyatamaṃ nivāsam
english: As they set out, the great seer Lomasha, with a joyful heart, having instructed them all like a father his sons, departed with a glad mind to the most sacred abode of the celestial beings.

sanskrit: tenānuśiṣṭārṣṭiṣeṇena caiva; tīrthāni ramyāṇi tapovanāni mahānti cānyāni sarāṃsi pārthāḥ; saṃpaśyamānāḥ prayayur narāgryāḥ
english: Thus instructed by him and also by Arishthishena, beholding the beautiful holy places, the hermitages, and other great lakes, the foremost of men, the sons of Pritha, journeyed onward.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nagottamaṃ prasravaṇair upetaṃ; diśāṃ gajaiḥ kiṃnarapakṣibhiś ca sukhaṃ nivāsaṃ jahatāṃ hi teṣāṃ; na prītir āsīd bharatarṣabhāṇām
english: Vaishampayana said: "As they left that excellent mountain endowed with springs and inhabited by the elephants of the directions, kinnara, and birds, those bulls of Bharata's line felt no pleasure in departing from that pleasant abode."

sanskrit: tatas tu teṣāṃ punar eva harṣaḥ; kailāsam ālokya mahān babhūva kuberakāntaṃ bharatarṣabhāṇāṃ; mahīdharaṃ vāridharaprakāśam
english: Then great joy arose in them once again as those bulls of Bharata's line beheld Mount Kailasa, beloved of Kubera, that mountain shining like a mass of clouds.

sanskrit: samucchrayān parvatasaṃnirodhān; goṣṭhān girīṇāṃ girisetumālāḥ bahūn prapātāṃś ca samīkṣya vīrāḥ; sthalāni nimnāni ca tatra tatra
english: The heroes beheld the towering peaks, the mountain passes, the mountain plateaus, the chains of mountain bridges, the many waterfalls, and the high and low ground here and there.

sanskrit: tathaiva cānyāni mahāvanāni; mṛgadvijānekapasevitāni ālokayanto 'bhiyayuḥ pratītās; te dhanvinaḥ khaḍgadharā narāgryāḥ
english: Likewise beholding other great forests frequented by deer, birds, and many ascetics, those foremost of men — archers and sword-bearers — advanced with confidence.

sanskrit: vanāni ramyāṇi sarāṃsi nadyo; guhā girīṇāṃ girigahvarāṇi ete nivāsāḥ satataṃ babhūvur; niśāniśaṃ prāpya nararṣabhāṇām
english: Beautiful forests, lakes, rivers, mountain caves, and mountain gorges — these became the ever-changing nightly dwelling places of those bulls among men, as they reached a new one each night.

sanskrit: te durgavāsaṃ bahudhā niruṣya; vyatītya kailāsam acintyarūpam āsedur atyarthamanoramaṃ vai; tam āśramāgryaṃ vṛṣaparvaṇas te
english: Having dwelt in many difficult mountain fastnesses and having passed beyond Kailasa of inconceivable beauty, they reached that most delightful of hermitages, that excellent ashrama of Vrishaparvan.

sanskrit: sametya rājñā vṛṣaparvaṇas te; pratyarcitās tena ca vītamohāḥ śaśaṃsire vistaraśaḥ pravāsaṃ; śivaṃ yathāvad vṛṣaparvaṇas te
english: Meeting with the king Vrishaparvan and being honoured by him, those who were free from delusion described in detail their auspicious sojourn to Vrishaparvan exactly as it had occurred.

sanskrit: sukhoṣitās tatra ta ekarātraṃ; puṇyāśrame devamaharṣijuṣṭe abhyāyayus te badarīṃ viśālāṃ; sukhena vīrāḥ punar eva vāsam
english: Having dwelt happily there for one night in that holy hermitage frequented by gods and great sages, those heroes easily went again to Badari, that vast and auspicious dwelling place.

sanskrit: ūṣus tatas tatra mahānubhāvā; nārāyaṇasthānagatā narāgryāḥ kuberakāntāṃ nalinīṃ viśokāḥ; saṃpaśyamānāḥ surasiddhajuṣṭām
english: Those foremost of men, of great majesty, having arrived at the abode of Narayana, dwelt there, free from sorrow, gazing upon the lake beloved of Kubera, frequented by the gods and siddhas.

sanskrit: tāṃ cātha dṛṣṭvā nalinīṃ viśokāḥ; pāṇḍoḥ sutāḥ sarvanarapravīrāḥ te remire nandanavāsam etya; dvijarṣayo vītabhayā yathaiva
english: And having seen that lake, the sons of Pandu — those foremost of all men — free from sorrow, sported as if they had come to dwell in Nandana, just as the twice-born seers free from fear.

sanskrit: tataḥ krameṇopayayur nṛvīrā; yathāgatenaiva pathā samagrāḥ vihṛtya māsaṃ sukhino badaryāṃ; kirātarājño viṣayaṃ subāhoḥ
english: Then those heroic men gradually approached, all together by the very road by which they had come, having sported happily at Badari for a month, the realm of Subahu the Kirata king.

sanskrit: cīnāṃs tukhārān daradān sadārvān; deśān kuṇindasya ca bhūriratnān atītya durgaṃ himavatpradeśaṃ; puraṃ subāhor dadṛśur nṛvīrāḥ
english: Passing through the lands of the Chinas, Tokharas, Daradas, Darvas, and the gem-rich territories of the Kunindas, and crossing the difficult Himalayan regions, those heroic men beheld the city of Subahu.

sanskrit: śrutvā ca tān pārthivaputrapautrān; prāptān subāhur viṣaye samagrān pratyudyayau prītiyutaḥ sa rājā; taṃ cābhyanandan vṛṣabhāḥ kurūṇām
english: Hearing that those sons and grandsons of kings had arrived in his territory altogether, king Subahu went forth joyfully to meet them; and the bulls of the Kurus welcomed him in return.

sanskrit: sametya rājñā tu subāhunā te; sūtair viśokapramukhaiś ca sarvaiḥ sahendrasenaiḥ paricārakaiś ca; paurogavair ye ca mahānasasthāḥ
english: Having met with king Subahu, and with all the bards headed by Vishoka, with Indrasena and the other attendants, and the stewards and those stationed in the royal kitchen —

sanskrit: sukhoṣitās tatra ta ekarātraṃ; sūtān upādāya rathāṃś ca sarvān ghaṭotkacaṃ sānucaraṃ visṛjya; tato 'bhyayur yāmunam adrirājam
english: — having dwelt there happily for one night, taking the charioteers and all the chariots, dismissing Ghatotkacha along with his followers, they then proceeded to the king of mountains on the Yamuna.

sanskrit: tasmin girau prasravaṇopapanne; himottarīyāruṇapāṇḍusānau viśākhayūpaṃ samupetya cakrus; tadā nivāsaṃ puruṣapravīrāḥ
english: On that mountain endowed with springs, on its slope reddened by the snow-laden northern winds and whitened in places, those foremost of men arrived at Vishakhayupa and made their dwelling there.

sanskrit: varāhanānāmṛgapakṣijuṣṭaṃ; mahad vanaṃ caitrarathaprakāśam śivena yātvā mṛgayāpradhānāḥ; saṃvatsaraṃ tatra vane vijahruḥ
english: In that great forest frequented by boars, various deer and birds, shining like the Chaitraratha garden, they passed, devoted chiefly to the hunt and going forth auspiciously, an entire year sporting in that forest.

sanskrit: tatrāsasādātibalaṃ bhujaṃgaṃ; kṣudhārditaṃ mṛtyum ivograrūpam vṛkodaraḥ parvatakandarāyāṃ; viṣādamohavyathitāntarātmā
english: There, in a mountain gorge, Vrikodara encountered an exceedingly powerful serpent, tormented by hunger and of a terrible form like Death itself — and his inner soul was afflicted with anguish and bewilderment.

sanskrit: dvīpo 'bhavad yatra vṛkodarasya; yudhiṣṭhiro dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ amokṣayad yas tam anantatejā; grāheṇa saṃveṣṭitasarvagātram
english: It was there that Yudhishthira, the most excellent of upholders of righteousness and of boundless energy, became a refuge for Vrikodara — he who freed him when every limb was coiled about by the serpent.

sanskrit: te dvādaśaṃ varṣam athopayāntaṃ; vane vihartuṃ kuravaḥ pratītāḥ tasmād vanāc caitrarathaprakāśāc; chriyā jvalantas tapasā ca yuktāḥ
english: As the twelfth year was now approaching, the Kurus, blazing with beauty and endowed with austerity, confident in their purpose, prepared to leave that forest which shone like the Chaitraratha garden and to roam in another.

sanskrit: tataś ca yātvā marudhanvapārśvaṃ; sadā dhanurvedaratipradhānāḥ sarasvatīm etya nivāsakāmāḥ; saras tato dvaitavanaṃ pratīyuḥ
english: Then, having gone to the edge of the desert, those ever-devoted chiefly to the science of archery, wishing to settle by the Sarasvati river, went thence to the lake and the Dvaitavana forest.

sanskrit: samīkṣya tān dvaitavane niviṣṭān; nivāsinas tatra tato 'bhijagmuḥ tapodamācārasamādhiyuktās; tṛṇodapātrāharaṇāśmakuṭṭāḥ
english: Seeing them settled in Dvaitavana, those who dwelt there came to them — those endowed with austerity, self-restraint, good conduct, and meditation, who collected grass, water, and vessels, and ground grain with stones.

sanskrit: plakṣākṣarauhītakavetasāś ca; snuhā badaryaḥ khadirāḥ śirīṣāḥ bilveṅgudāḥ pīluśamīkarīrāḥ; sarasvatītīraruhā babhūvuḥ
english: Plaksha, Aksha, Rohitaka, Vetasa, Snuhi, Badari, Khadira, Shirisha, Bilva, Inguda, Pilu, Shami, and Karira — these grew along the banks of the Sarasvati.

sanskrit: tāṃ yakṣagandharvamaharṣikāntām; āyāgabhūtām iva devatānām sarasvatīṃ prītiyutāś carantaḥ; sukhaṃ vijahrur naradevaputrāḥ
english: Roaming joyfully along that Sarasvati beloved of yakshas, gandharvas, and great sages — like a place of worship for the gods — the sons of the lord of men sported happily.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ nāgāyutaprāṇo bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ bhayam āhārayat tīvraṃ tasmād ajagarān mune
english: Janamejaya said: "How did Bhimasena of mighty strength, whose vitality equals ten thousand elephants, come to experience such intense fear from that python-serpent, O sage?"

sanskrit: paulastyaṃ yo ''hvayad yuddhe dhanadaṃ baladarpitaḥ nalinyāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtvā varāṇāṃ yakṣarakṣasām
english: "He who in battle challenged Dhanada of the Paulastya lineage, proud of his strength, and made havoc among the excellent yakshas and rakshasas at the Nalini lake —"

sanskrit: taṃ śaṃsasi bhayāviṣṭam āpannam arikarṣaṇam etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: "— you speak of him as seized with fear and fallen into distress, that crusher of enemies. This is what I wish to hear — for my curiosity is very great."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bahvāścarye vane teṣāṃ vasatām ugradhanvinām prāptānām āśramād rājan rājarṣer vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: "While those mighty archers were dwelling in that forest of many wonders, O king, having come from the hermitage of the royal sage Vrishaparvan —"

sanskrit: yadṛcchayā dhanuṣpāṇir baddhakhaḍgo vṛkodaraḥ dadarśa tad vanaṃ ramyaṃ devagandharvasevitam
english: "— Vrikodara, bow in hand, sword girt at his side, wandering by chance, beheld that beautiful forest frequented by gods and gandharvas."

sanskrit: sa dadarśa śubhān deśān girer himavatas tadā devarṣisiddhacaritān apsarogaṇasevitān
english: He then beheld the beautiful regions of the Himalaya mountains, frequented by divine sages and siddhas, served by hosts of apsaras.

sanskrit: cakoraiś cakravākaiś ca pakṣibhir jīvajīvakaiḥ kokilair bhṛṅgarājaiś ca tatra tatra vināditān
english: Resounding here and there with chakoras, chakravakas, jivajivaka birds, kokilas, and bhrinarajas —

sanskrit: nityapuṣpaphalair vṛkṣair himasaṃsparśakomalaiḥ upetān bahulacchāyair manonayananandanaiḥ
english: — filled with trees that bore perennial flowers and fruits, made soft by the touch of snow, with abundant shade, delighting the mind and eye —

sanskrit: sa saṃpaśyan girinadīr vaiḍūryamaṇisaṃnibhaiḥ salilair himasaṃsparśair haṃsakāraṇḍavāyutaiḥ
english: — he gazed upon the mountain rivers with their waters resembling vaidurya gems, cool to the touch with snow, thronged with swans and karandava ducks —

sanskrit: vanāni devadārūṇāṃ meghānām iva vāgurāḥ haricandanamiśrāṇi tuṅgakālīyakāny api
english: — forests of deodar cedars like snares for clouds, mixed with harichandana trees, and tall kaliyaka trees as well —

sanskrit: mṛgayāṃ paridhāvan sa sameṣu marudhanvasu vidhyan mṛgāñ śaraiḥ śuddhaiś cacāra sumahābalaḥ
english: — that one of very great strength ranged about, running through the hunt across the level windswept plains, piercing deer with his pure arrows.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahākāyaṃ bhujaṅgaṃ lomaharṣaṇam giridurge samāpannaṃ kāyenāvṛtya kandaram
english: He beheld a serpent of enormous body, causing the hair to stand on end, settled in a mountain fastness, its body filling a cavern.

sanskrit: parvatābhogavarṣmāṇaṃ bhogaiś candrārkamaṇḍalaiḥ citrāṅgam ajinaiś citrair haridrāsadṛśacchavim
english: Its body was as massive as a mountain's bulk; its coils were like the orbs of the moon and sun; variegated in markings, with mottled skin, its hue was like that of turmeric.

sanskrit: guhākāreṇa vaktreṇa caturdaṃṣṭreṇa rājatā dīptākṣeṇātitāmreṇa lihantaṃ sṛkkiṇī muhuḥ
english: With its mouth like the entrance of a cave, four-fanged and gleaming silver, with blazing eyes of a deep copper hue, it repeatedly licked the corners of its lips.

sanskrit: trāsanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālāntakayamopamam niḥśvāsakṣveḍanādena bhartsayantam iva sthitam
english: It stood there terrifying all living beings, comparable to Death and the end-of-age Yama, as if threatening them with the sound of its hissing and screeching.
